findings.title: Busy flag may stick when Publish fails
findings.message: The goroutine reads request.Color and calls w.Context() off the UI thread; if ticket.Publish fails (window closed) NativeColorBusy is never reset on the owner, leaving the button disabled forever. Publish error is discarded.
findings.suggestion: Handle Publish error and reset NativeColorBusy when it fails.

findings.title: Add edit relies solely on post-validation
findings.message: GradientAdd with duplicate stop ID is only rejected by Validate after the fact (fine), but GradientRemove/Move with e.StopID empty for Add is fine. More notably, in Apply, if two stops share the same ID the loop picks the last index; Validate would reject, so OK. The real issue: GradientAdd does not clamp e.Stop.Position/validate color, relying only on final Validate, which accepts positions in [0,1]; acceptable. Low impact.
findings.suggestion: Explicitly validate e.Stop.Position finiteness and range before append for clearer errors.

findings.title: Tie ordering on equal positions
findings.message: Stable sort with equal positions: when a moved stop lands on the same position as another, order among equals depends on prior slice order, so dragged handle may jump across equals, contradicting 'ordered hard transition' identity expectations.
findings.suggestion: Document or tie-break by prior index of the moved stop.

finding.title: Accessibility 'press' mutates value; unclamped set
finding.message: Handles can cross while dragging and Apply re-sorts stops, but TrackInput.Handles ordering is assumed sorted elsewhere. In the non-gradient branch, Handles[0] and Handles[len-1] are used as range ends; fine when sorted. However Accessibility 'set' computes fraction with (v-Min)/(Max-Min) without clamping, so out-of-range values are passed to Set (clamped later). Lower risk, but accessibility 'press' also increments, which silently mutates the value on a plain press.
finding.suggestion: Do not map 'press' to a value-changing increment; clamp the set fraction explicitly.
